pull.title: MINOR: Add tests that tagged fields are written in ascending tag order
pull.body:
Add tests that tagged fields are written in ascending tag order

Reviewers: Shay Elkin (github:shayelkin), TengYao Chi
 <frankvicky@apache.org>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body:
I don't think this tests what we expect: it verifies that the tags are written in the order they are added, which is not the same as ascending tag order.

The right properties to validate are:
1. The tags are indeed in the expected order, which can be checked multiple ways. For example, that or every two consecutive tags `t1, t2` in the message, `t1 < t2`, or that sorting the tags keeps their order the same, and there are no duplicates.
2. And that all tags in expectedTags were written to the message.
LGTM, but you need a proper review from a comitter to merge this.
The remaining gap (a schema with non-contiguous tags to exercise the interleaving path in the generated writer) can go in a follow-up along with the RawTaggedFieldWriter test.

review_comments.body:
> since RawTaggedFieldWriter rejects an unsorted list.

If we don't have an explicit test for that, it'd be useful to add one as a follow up PR.
nit: I would drop the KIP reference here; the KIP number belongs in the PR description rather than in source comments.

I don't think the randomization buys us anything here. 
The write order is fixed at code-generation time, and the setters each touch an independent field, so the order in which they are called cannot affect the output. 
Randomly choosing a subset of tags only toggles independent `if` blocks.

A deterministic `@ParameterizedTest` over versions 1 and 2 that sets every known tagged field (8 for v1, 10 for v2) plus a few unknown tags would verify the same property without the 100-iteration loop and the seed plumbing.

This statement isn't true in general. 
Unknown tags can be lower than the highest known tag.
for example, in version 1 of this message tags 8 and 9 are unknown, and a schema may have gaps between its tags.

That matters for coverage. The generator interleaves unknown tags between known ones by emitting `_rawWriter.writeRawTags(_writable, <nextKnownTag>)` wherever there is a gap. `SimpleExampleMessage` has contiguous tags 0-9, so the generated writer only calls `writeRawTags(_writable, Integer.MAX_VALUE)` at the very end, and this test only exercises that trailing path. I checked the production schemas under `clients/src/main/resources/common/message` and none of them has a tag gap either, so the interleaving path has no test anywhere in the repo.

If the goal is "tags are written in ascending order", the two cases worth adding are:
1. version 1 with `RawTaggedField`s for tags 8 and 9, asserting they are written after tag 7;
2. a test schema with a gap in its tags (either a new field in `SimpleExampleMessage.json` or a small dedicated schema), with unknown tags placed inside the gap.

These two assertions can be collapsed into one that is also stricter:

```java
assertEquals(expectedTags.stream().sorted().toList(), writtenTags);
```

If you do want to keep randomness, `TestUtils.SEEDED_RANDOM` is what the rest of the clients tests use.
`System.nanoTime()` seeds make a failure non-reproducible unless someone copies the seed out of the log.
